label: prf:positive-definite-dagger
title: Proof that the Frobenius dagger is positive-definite
html:
Write \langle a, b\rangle = \int_A \mu(a \otimes b) for the Frobenius pairing, non-degenerate by Frobenius pairing exists. Throughout, R \cong \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1}) is the formally-real ordered field and S is the pivotal self-adjoint antipode of the hypotheses.

A positive-definite dagger structure requires two things: that \dagger is an involution, and that f^{\dagger} \circ f is strictly positive for every non-zero f. We verify each in turn.

Involutivity. Because the antipode is pivotal, S^2 = \mathrm{id}. Expanding (f^{\dagger})^{\dagger} = \int_A \mu(S(f^{\dagger}) \otimes -) and applying S^2 = \mathrm{id} together with Frobenius associativity \int_A \mu(\mu \otimes \mathrm{id}) = \int_A \mu(\mathrm{id} \otimes \mu) gives (f^{\dagger})^{\dagger} = f. Contravariance (g \circ f)^{\dagger} = f^{\dagger} \circ g^{\dagger} follows because S is an anti-homomorphism. Hence \dagger is an involutive structure.

Positive-definiteness. For non-zero f \colon \mathbf{1} \to X,

  f^{\dagger} \circ f
  = \int_A \mu(S(f) \otimes f)
  = \langle f, f\rangle \in \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1}) \cong R.

By the self-adjoint hypothesis S = \dagger, the pairing evaluates f against its own adjoint, so \langle f, f\rangle = s^2 is a square in R (the categorical norm-square of f). Non-degeneracy of the pairing forces \langle f, f\rangle \neq 0 whenever f \neq 0. In a formally-real ordered field a non-zero square is strictly positive, so f^{\dagger} \circ f > 0. Therefore \dagger is a positive-definite involutive structure.

This is the categorical Frobenius-norm / GNS positivity construction ([kock2004], Ch. 2). The three hypotheses are exactly the inputs the argument consumes: non-degeneracy gives \langle f, f\rangle \neq 0, the pivotal adjoint identification gives the square, and formal reality turns a non-zero square into a positive element. \square
